$comment: Non-secret project settings, one section per module (lib/config.mjs). Every other section still reads from its legacy file (jev.config.json, scripts/review-config.json, …): a section this file lacks falls back to that file alone. Do NOT add a `jev.rails` key here — this file wins per TOP-LEVEL key, so it would replace jev.config.json's whole `rails` object and silently turn the promoted review and prose rails off (semantic-lint C1).

lint.$comment: semantic-lint rules (Roadmap/09-platform-infra/semantic-lint). Each rule's globs, allowlist and patterns SELECT candidate hunks deterministically; Jev is asked one question per selected hunk. Its mode, threshold and shadowExpires live in jev.config.json → rails.lint. Wording measured with `node scripts/jev-eval.mjs --live --rail lint` — see the question's $measured.

rules.source: AGENTS.md rule 1 (the growth engine owns telemetry; never build a parallel pipeline)

question.$measured: 2026-09-30, jev-1.13.0, the 33 lint fixtures in scripts/jev-eval.fixtures.json (16 real candidates the selector picks from 220 commits of main, all clean; 17 constructed, 14 of them violations), threshold 0.8. v1 (one sentence, generic yes/no criteria): decided 23/33, 23 right; unsure on product code READING events/features, an ops-timing table and <Analytics /> on its own. v2 (this wording: names reads for the product's own screens, ops timings, feature toggles, ad-hoc funnel queries and rendering a vendor component): decided 30/33, 30 right. Undecided: one read (0.22) and two violations (0.73 analytics.track in a server action, 0.70 a features update). Re-asking identical hunks moved p by up to 0.04 between runs. The threshold was NOT fitted to these 33 cases; that is the shadow period's job. Re-measure before changing a word: node scripts/jev-eval.mjs --live --rail lint.
question.instructions: This is one hunk from a git diff in a Next.js + Supabase product whose growth engine owns all product telemetry. Events are ingested only by POST /api/v1/track and features registered only by /api/v1/features/sync (both through the @golden-frijoles/sdk client); funnels, conversion, retention, North Star and experiment results are computed only by the canonical query libraries. Does this hunk start a parallel telemetry pipeline, a second path that collects, stores, ships or analyses product-usage events?

criteria.true: Yes, any of: a new table, view or migration that stores user actions, clicks, page views, usage or analytics events under any name; an insert, update or delete on the events or features tables (including toggling a feature's enabled flag) outside those two ingest routes; a route or query that computes funnels, conversion, retention or other usage metrics from raw events instead of the canonical query libraries; importing, calling or rendering a third-party analytics SDK or component (PostHog, Segment, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Google Analytics or gtag, dataLayer, Vercel Analytics' <Analytics />, analytics.track and the like); or a beacon or fetch that ships events to any other collector.
criteria.false: No, when it is any of: tracking through the engine's own SDK client or /api/v1/track; a plain read of the events or features tables that lists, displays or checks them for the product's own screens, catalog, tasks, reports or signals, without computing usage metrics; a table, route or call for another purpose (auth, tokens, billing, flags, deliveries, experiments' own registry and decisions, scenarios, content); operational measurements of the product's own performance, such as query timings; or a comment, string or name that only mentions analytics or tracking.
